reason: Reproduced in Chromium with forcedColors active, 1440x960, state=owner-flight. .b-rail paints rgba(255,255,255,0.16) on a white Canvas: invisible. .b-todayRule computes rgb(255,255,255) on white: invisible. Every tick collapses to one Canvas fill with a CanvasText ring, indigo lead included. The screenshot shows a page with no spine, no today and no next. Zero forced-colors blocks in b.css, shell.css or master.html. Windows contrast themes are where the desktop owner builds, and a hue-free hierarchy has nothing left to degrade to.
sharpenedFix: One @media (forced-colors: active) block at the end of b.css. Drop forced-color-adjust: none: it opts elements out of the user's palette, and system-colour declarations inside the block are honoured without it. Map the design's own logic. Structure to CanvasText (.b-rail background: CanvasText). Accent to Highlight (.b-todayRule background: Highlight, height 2px; lead and anchor ticks background and border-color: Highlight). Ordinary ticks background: Canvas with a 1px CanvasText ring, so filled versus hollow still means this one. Cover the .b-back and [data-accent="structure"] variants. Add a forcedColors pass over the state matrix in interaction-check.mjs asserting rail, today rule and lead tick each paint a non-Canvas fill, and re-run audit.mjs to confirm system keywords clear the palette lock.
